testing_note: Walked the skill by hand through a scratch five-item travel claim (taxi with a tip, client dinner with wine over a per-person meal cap, hotel receipt that includes an unclaimed minibar charge, lunch with no receipt, lounge pass the policy does not mention). Three gaps surfaced and were fixed: Approve now allows a reduced amount for partial exclusions (tip, alcohol), not only caps; Approve covers items where the policy waives the receipt; receipt matching now reads itemised lines so a receipt total that differs from the claim is not misread as a contradiction.
applied_note: I made it model-invoked with a short description that front-loads the leading word (expense claim) and lists only distinct trigger branches, and kept everything in one SKILL.md because every branch needs the verdict definitions, steps and output template, so there was nothing worth disclosing. The three verdicts and the evidence rule are co-located as reference above the steps, each step ends on a checkable, exhaustive completion criterion ('every line item has a verdict, an approved amount, and its evidence'), and the constraints are phrased positively (the supplied policy is the whole rulebook; an open item is a finished verdict paired with a question) rather than as prohibitions.
